verses.1: Then, in the twelfth year, Shatrughna, accompanied by a small retinue of servants and army, desired to go to Ayodhya, which was protected by Rama.
verses.2: Then, having sent back his chief ministers and military commanders, he proceeded with excellent horses and a hundred chariots.
verses.3: Having traveled for seven or eight counted days, the greatly renowned Shatrughna, the delight of the Raghus, arrived at Valmiki's hermitage and made his stay there.
verses.4: Then, the best among men, Shatrughna, having saluted Valmiki's feet, accepted the water for washing feet, the respectful offering, and the hospitality from the sage's hand.
verses.5: That sage narrated thousands of stories, varied in form and very sweet, to the great-souled Shatrughna.
verses.6: And the sage spoke words concerning the killing of Lavana, saying that the deed of killing Lavana, which you accomplished, was extremely arduous.
verses.7: O gentle and mighty-armed one, many very powerful kings, along with their armies and vehicles, were killed by Lavana while fighting him.
verses.8: O best among men, that wicked one was killed by you with ease, and the fear of the world was pacified by your valor.
verses.9: The terrible killing of Ravana was accomplished with great effort, but this very great deed was done by you effortlessly.
verses.10: Upon Lavana's death, great joy arose among the gods and all beings, and good was done for the entire world.
verses.11: O best among men, O Raghava, that battle was seen by me exactly as it happened, while I was seated in the assembly of Indra.
verses.12: O Shatrughna, supreme joy also resides in my heart, and I will kiss your head, for this is the highest expression of affection.
verses.13: Having thus spoken and kissed Shatrughna on the head, the great sage offered hospitality to him and his followers.
verses.14: After eating, the best among men, Shatrughna, heard the excellent sweetness of the song narrating the deeds of Rama, in due order at that time.
verses.15: At that time, he heard the previously composed deeds of Rama, which were endowed with the rhythm of string instruments, accompanied by actions in three registers, refined, characterized by rules, and perfectly rhythmic.
verses.16: Having heard those true words, which recounted events exactly as they had formerly happened, Rama, the tiger among men, became bewildered with tearful eyes.
verses.17: For a moment, he remained as if bewildered, sighing repeatedly, and in that song, he heard the past events as if they were unfolding in the present.
verses.18: And the king's followers, having heard that excellent song, became downcast and distressed, exclaiming, "This is indeed a wonder!"
verses.19: And the soldiers present there spoke to each other, wondering, "What is this? Where are we? Is this a dream vision?"
verses.20: They wondered if what they were hearing in the hermitage, which seemed to be a previously seen event, was a dream or a beautiful song.
verses.21: Filled with great astonishment, they said to Shatrughna, "O best among men, please properly ask Valmiki, the foremost among sages."
verses.22: But Shatrughna said to all the curious soldiers, "O soldiers, it is not proper for us to make such inquiries here."
verses.23: Many wonders occur here in this sage's hermitage, but it is not proper to question that great sage out of mere curiosity.
verses.24: Having thus spoken that statement to the soldiers, Shatrughna then saluted the great sage and returned to his own camp. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे एकसप्ततिमः सर्गः ।। 71 ।। Thus ends the seventy-first sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
